newsitem.title: USA: Compaq sets stock buyback, shares rise.
newsitem.headline: Compaq sets stock buyback, shares rise.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. said Thursday it would tap into its nearly $5 billion cash reserve to buy back up to 25 million shares of stock.
The announcement sent the stock jumping, but did nothing to dampen speculation that the computer giant is in a mood for acquisitions.
Chairman Ben Rosen said at Compaq's annual shareholder meeting the buyback would encompass "roughly 9 percent" of the company's 274.5 million outstanding shares of common stock.
Compaq stock closed up $2.625 at $80.125 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Chief Executive Officer Eckhard Pfeiffer told Reuters after the meeting the buyback would not affect the company's ability to make acquisitions, particularly stock-for-stock deals.

Compaq recently purchased Microcom Inc. for $280 million and has had merger talks with Micron Electronics Inc. and, according to unconfirmed rumours, Gateway 2000 Inc. Computer Reseller News reported in its online edition Wednesday that Compaq is attempting to finalise a deal for Micron.
Micron's stock was up $1.34 to $20.50 on the Nasdaq on the report.
Pfeiffer would not comment on any possible transactions.

Speculation about a Compaq buying spree has increased because of its cash position, which Rosen said strong earnings had pushed to nearly $5 billion, and its move toward build-to-order sales to compete with Dell Computer Corp. and Gateway.

Some analysts believe Compaq may be in the market for a company already doing build-to-order so that it can jump into the market quickly. Pfeiffer said U.S. customers would be able to custom-order Compaq computers "before this quarter's over."

Compaq's competitive position with Dell, based in Austin, Texas, prompted several shareholder questions at the meeting. They wondered why Dell, despite Compaq's enormous success in past years, had a higher price-to-earnings ratio.

"Knowing what our plans are for the rest of the year and next year, I think we will be accorded the recognition that I think we deserve as the Street begins to see the efficiencies we've implemented," Rosen said.
About the buyback, Compaq said the stock would be bought in open market or private transactions from time to time.
It also said its board approved a cash offer for $300 million of the company's outstanding bonds.
